The manual sets the 80-point floor only for nationals of the notified countries who hold B-1, B-2, C-1, C-3, C-4, D-3, E-9, E-10 or G-1. That list is closed and does not include D-4, so any D-4 holder with a degree changes at 60 points. The rest of the note (1 year in total, 3 years at 80+) is correct. verified-by-review.md #2 already marks this WRONG and says the same text on D-2-5 (line 457) and F-3 (line 1306) is wrong too. Those two are outside this finding but need the same edit. The note is plain text with no gating, so the fix is only a text change.

verdicts.reason: The repo claim holds: I recomputed in-degrees with js-yaml and no 'next' list, NONE's included, contains D-4-2. Its six outgoing edges are therefore dead, and verified-by-review #6 lists it as unreachable. The status is real: a reproduction of the manual describes 졸업생에 대한 일반연수(D-4-2) for 국내대학(전문대 포함) 졸업예정자, and D-4-2 is also issued from abroad to inviting companies' staff. The fix as written does not work in this repo for two reasons. First, data/visadocs.yaml gives D-4-2 only an 'extend' list (K-Trainee D-4-2K), with no 'abroad' and no 'change' list. Both new edges would break the edge/document invariant that verified-by-review lists as correct, and the step would show no documents. Second, the in-Korea D-2-to-D-4-2 route is backed only by a secondary reproduction that may be from an older edition. I could not read the 2026 manual text for it because WebFetch could not reach any site and the search budget ran out. Also, `abroad: true` on a NONE move is redundant, and the new note must be written in all four languages.

verdicts.reason: The claim holds. D-4-3 has `next: [D-2-1, D-2-2]`, and both the manual and a 2025 MOJ press release (still in force: the 2026.9.18 manual has chapter 38, and the repo's D-10-1 change list has a 'Foreign youth raised in Korea (18-24)' variant) allow a Korean-school graduate aged 18-24 to change to D-10 with no points test and up to 3 years. D-10-1's needs already include {koreanEdu: 1, ageUnder: 25}, so the edge needs no needs override, and D-10-1 has a change list. The fix needs three changes. (a) The note must be in all four languages. (b) It should give the full condition: 7+ years in Korea before 18 and Korean elementary, middle and high school (or the equivalent exams). (c) It only works for real readers if D-4-3 also gets `gives: {koreanEdu: 1}` (see d4#5). The education checkbox reads 'From a Korean university', so a reader who honestly answers 'High school' gets koreanEdu = 0. All three D-10-1 needs branches then return 'no' and the new edge is blocked.

Treat it as one instance of a file-wide inconsistency.

verdicts.reason: D-4-3 has no 'gives'. The engine's factsAt() applies the 'gives' of every visa up to and including the one a step leaves from. Without it, two kinds of reader get wrong results. A school student who honestly answers 'Highest completed education: Below high school' (edu 0) is blocked from D-2-1/D-2-2 (needs edu:1), so D-4-3 shows nothing open. This is reproduced by visa-map-audit/tools/sim.mjs case F1: 'no' becomes 'yes' with the fix. A graduate who answers 'High school' cannot honestly tick the only Korea checkbox, which reads 'From a Korean university'. profileFacts() then sets koreanEdu = 0, which blocks the Korean-school routes D-10-1 {koreanEdu: 1, ageUnder: 25} and E-7-Y {koreanEdu: 1}. 'gives' is the only way the engine can learn about Korean schooling. Every step out of D-4-3 assumes the person finished Korean high school, so {edu: 1, koreanEdu: 1} is what the person has after completing D-4-3, as engine.md requires. One residual approximation is already present in the targets' needs: koreanEdu 1 cannot express 'all of elementary, middle and high school plus 7 years before 18'. The notes (d4#2) have to carry that.
